title: Case: Consignee wants to collect a pallet that has been sitting at the local depot for two days
context: Tallowmere Goods order TG-948, a cast-iron range cooker on one pallet, is travelling as DL-948 and is booked as a kerbside delivery. The consignee account and shipment match are verified.
initial_request: Three days. THREE days I have rung and been told a computer will email me when it feels like it. The cooker is fifteen minutes from my house, I know it is because the lorry drove past the end of my road on Tuesday. The fitter is booked for Saturday and won't hold the date. I am not asking for anything difficult. Give me the address of the depot and I will be there by one o'clock today with a trailer and my passport. That is all. Just the address.

events.body: DL-948, one pallet (range cooker, TG-948), arrived at the destination depot 21 July 09:30. The depot is a subcontractor site: Kessel Yard, Unit 4, Marrow Lane. It does not take walk-in collections without a release note issued by the depot. The collection email to the consignee is generated by the depot system when the release note is issued. Site details are for internal use until then.
Tracker says it's at the local depot. Can I just come and get it? I have a trailer and two people to lift.

events.from: Customer care line, Plover Arc Logistics
events.body: Agent: I can't give out the depot address until the collection email has gone to you. Caller: When does that go? Agent: I don't have a time for that. Caller: So who sends it? Agent: It's automatic.

events.from: Customer care line, Plover Arc Logistics
events.body: Caller: Third day ringing. Has the email gone? Agent: Not yet. Caller: Can you send it? Agent: I'm not able to trigger it from here. Caller: Can you tell me where the depot is? Agent: Not until the email has gone.

DL-948 is on the floor, bay 6. Not released. It's booked kerbside delivery, consignee collection was never on the booking, so no release note and no email. We can convert it to collection if the Freight planner or the desk asks us on this queue. Then we check we can release to the named consignee, issue the note and the email goes with the ID she needs to bring. Nobody has asked.

Three days. THREE days I have rung and been told a computer will email me when it feels like it. The cooker is fifteen minutes from my house, I know it is because the lorry drove past the end of my road on Tuesday. The fitter is booked for Saturday and won't hold the date. I am not asking for anything difficult. Give me the address of the depot and I will be there by one o'clock today with a trailer and my passport. That is all. Just the address.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask the depot to convert DL-948 from kerbside delivery to consignee collection, confirm it can release to the named consignee, and issue the release note and collection email.

must: Asks the depot on its work queue to convert DL-948 to consignee collection and, if it can release to Bettina Roake, to issue the release note and collection email.
Asks the depot to confirm the outcome and when she can collect, leaving the release decision with the depot.
Tells the depot she has rung three days running without anyone raising the conversion, and that a fitter is booked for Saturday, so the request is handled today.
must_not: Gives the consignee the depot's name, address or location before the depot has issued the release note.
Tells her she can collect today or at one o'clock, or that the pallet has been released.
Promises delivery or collection before Saturday.
Tells her to keep waiting for the automatic email without acting on why it has not been sent.
Offers compensation or a refund of delivery charges.
expected.reference_message: Request on DL-948 (one pallet, range cooker, TG-948), bay 6. Please convert this from kerbside delivery to consignee collection. The consignee, Bettina Roake, has asked to collect it herself; she has a trailer and help to lift, and says she can bring photo ID. Please check you can release to her as the named consignee and, if so, issue the release note so the collection email goes out with your site details and ID requirements. Please confirm to me either way, and the earliest time she can come. For priority: she has rung Customer care on each of the last three days and was told to wait for an email that could not be sent because nobody had asked you for the conversion, and she has a fitter booked for Saturday. I have not given her your address and have not told her she can collect; I will wait for your confirmation.

rationale: She is demanding a subcontractor site's address, which the desk must not hand out and which would not get her the pallet anyway: the depot releases nothing without its own release note. The depot has said the email is stuck because nobody asked for the conversion, and that the desk may ask on its queue. The desk makes that request and lets the depot decide and disclose.

review.note: Coordinator asked the depot on its work queue to convert to collection and withheld the site address, matching the key.
